title: Electrical injury
summary: Disconnect power safely, avoid contact until the source is isolated, and assess for cardiac arrest and burns.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Electrical Injury
WHO Basic Emergency Care: Approach to the Acutely Ill and Injured
actions: Do not touch the person until the power source is isolated. Turn off mains power or have the utility disconnect a high-voltage line.
Call emergency services for high-voltage exposure, lightning, loss of consciousness, breathing difficulty, chest pain, abnormal heartbeat, or significant burns.
When safe, check responsiveness and breathing. Start CPR and use an AED if breathing is absent or abnormal.
Cool visible thermal burns with clean running water and cover loosely after cooling. Electrical injury may be severe beneath small skin marks.
Keep the person still and monitor until help arrives.
prohibitions: Do not approach fallen power lines or an energized vehicle.
Do not use a wet or metal object to move a live wire.
Do not apply ice, ointment, or home remedies to burns.

emergencyCall.text: High-voltage, lightning, loss of consciousness, abnormal breathing, chest symptoms, or significant burns requires emergency services.
